commits.message: [expo] Use Hermes TextDecoder and remove the UTF-8 polyfill (#50853)
commits.author: savv
commits.pr_title: [expo] Use Hermes TextDecoder and remove the UTF-8 polyfill
commits.pr_body:
# Why

Follow-up to #41672: RN 0.88 now includes Hermes TextDecoder, so Expo should stop replacing it with its UTF-8-only implementation (which breaks Latin-1 consumers such as jsPDF/fast-png). Related: #48790 retains a fallback; this PR removes it completely for SDK 58.

# How

Delete `TextDecoder.ts`, its global registration, and its standalone tests; Hermes owns decoder conformance coverage. Keep Expo’s TextDecoderStream coverage on both native Jest presets. Combine the encoding documentation with links to both Hermes implementations, and link the changeset to facebook/hermes#1855. Custom JS runtimes must provide TextDecoder before Expo initializes.

# Test Plan

- `packages/expo`: after the review changes, `jest --runInBand --watchman=false src/winter` — 21 suites / 308 tests passed, 4 existing skips; includes expo/fetch and both encoding streams. Typecheck, lint, and changeset formatting passed. Standalone TextDecoder tests were removed as requested.
- GT integration: applied the complete removal to SDK 58 preview.6 / RN 0.88 RC1 in existing iOS 27 simulator and Android emulator binaries. Verified native decoder identity, Latin-1/UTF-16/UTF-8, split UTF-8 and fatal errors; expo/fetch text/JSON/arrayBuffer/clone and streaming through TextDecoderStream; jsPDF PNG embedding, PDF creation/persistence, and GT App imports. The temporary bare-app harness explicitly loads `expo/virtual/streams`; no new native build was needed for this JS-only change.
- Docs: production/normal li

commits.message: chore(workflows): Allow "Version Packages" PRs to be merged "early" pushing waiting to publish tasks (#50928)
commits.author: kitten
commits.pr_title: chore(workflows): Allow "Version Packages" PRs to be merged "early" pushing waiting to publish tasks
commits.pr_body:
# Why

The `precompile-android` task can currently take 30+min, which exposed a weakness of precompiling in "Version Packages" PR workflows on EAS. While we can fall back to the publish runner, and let precompiling finish there, that's strictly slower. However, waiting 30+min to merge can be impossible if new changes come in too quickly.

We instead would like to merge any time the PR is fresh and then let the publish task wait for precompiling to finish. While sequencing EAS to GitHub or invoking from GitHub CI would be possible here, the cleaner approach is to (optionally) wait on the precompile task in GitHub.

# How

- Install `eas-cli` in `stable-publish`
- Wait on EAS workflows to finish when publishing
- Adjust EAS workflows to not cancel when new "Version Packages" PRs are opened

# Test Plan

- Can only be tested fully by running a release

# Why

expo/eas-cli#4433 enables the embedded bundle upload by default for projects on SDK 58 and later, controlled by `EAS_UPDATE_UPLOAD_EMBEDDED_BUNDLE`. On SDK 57 and below the feature stays experimental and opt-in via `EAS_UPDATE_EXPERIMENTAL_UPLOAD_EMBEDDED_BUNDLE`. The bundle diffing guide needs to match.

# How

- Split "Patches from the embedded bundle" into tabs: **SDK 58 and later** (on by default, shows how to disable with `EAS_UPDATE_UPLOAD_EMBEDDED_BUNDLE: "0"`) and **SDK 57 and below** (keeps the experimental note and the existing `EAS_UPDATE_EXPERIMENTAL_UPLOAD_EMBEDDED_BUNDLE: "1"` opt-in).
- Updated the intro paragraph and the "Current limitations" bullet so they no longer describe fresh-install patches as opt-in only.

[cli][metro-config][router-server][server] Unify static and streaming CSS assets (#50016)

# Why

Streaming rendering currently splits bundled, external, and inline CSS
separately, losing the order provided by Metro and changing the CSS
cascade.

# How

Use a single ordered array of structured CSS assets across both
rendering paths, which preserves the order as specified by Metro.

Other related changes:

- Metro doesn't generate unused link markup for external CSS; tag
emission is handled by each renderer directly
- Keeps support for SDK55+ server manifests which still separate CSS and
external CSS assets

# Why

Fixes #50816.

On Android, assets moved with `Album.create(name, assets, true)` or
`album.add` sometimes disappear from the media library. The file ends up
in the album folder, but its MediaStore row is deleted, so galleries and

`MediaStorePermissionsDelegate.hasWritePermissionForUri` checked write

app created would show a write request it doesn't need.

commits.message: [android][camera] Fix window staying white when CameraView unmounts during shutter animation (#50950)
commits.author: alanjhughes
commits.pr_title: [android][camera] Fix window staying white when CameraView unmounts during shutter animation
commits.pr_body:
# Why
Closes #50904

With animateShutter on, unmounting a CameraView right after takePictureAsync() can leave the whole window covered in solid white on Android.  The app still works underneath the white layer, but the user cannot see it.

# How

The shutter flash sets a white foreground on the root view, then clears it 50 ms later. The old code called rootView again inside each delayed runnable. While the camera view is attached, rootView is the DecorView. Once it detaches, rootView returns the camera view itself. If the view detached between the set and the clear, the clear went to the camera view and the DecorView stayed white.

I moved the flash into a flashShutter function in FlashShutter.kt. It reads rootView once, then sets and clears the foreground on that same view.

# Test Plan
I added FlashShutterTest. One test checks the normal flash. The other removes the camera view between the set and the clear, then checks that the DecorView foreground is null.

- Before the fix, the detach test failed with expected null, but was: ColorDrawable.
- After the fix, both tests pass

I also tested in bare-expo on a physical Pixel 7a (Android 17). I took pictures and then left the camera screen right after each capture. The window did not stay white.

commits.author: alanjhughes
commits.pr_title: [android][dev-launcher] Request the local network permission
commits.pr_body:
# Why

On Android 17, an app that declares this permission no longer gets it automatically, so the app must ask for it. #50057 added the prompt to ReactActivityDelegateWrapper.onCreate, and dev-launcher goes through that wrapper too. But the prompt runs only when no handler replaces the delegate.
  - In app mode, dev-launcher returns the same wrapper, so the prompt runs.
  - In launcher mode, dev-launcher returns DevLauncherReactActivityRedirectDelegate, and the wrapper calls that delegate's onCreate. The redirect delegate does not ask for the permission.

A development build always starts in launcher mode. The launcher fetches the manifest before it switches to app mode. So NSD discovery and the manifest request both run without the permission, and they fail before the code from #50057 can run.

# How

- LocalNetworkPermission: a new helper. It asks for the permission on Android 17 and later when the app does not have it. It asks at most once for each app process, so a denial at startup does not cause a second prompt on the launcher screen.
- DevLauncherReactActivityRedirectDelegate: This handles MainActivity in launcher mode, for deep links and for reopening the last app. It asks for the permission first and redirects after the user answers. If the user denies, it redirects anyway, so the app does not get stuck.
- DevLauncherActivity: It asks for the permission when the launcher opens. If the user grants it, NSD discovery restarts, because the first attempt fail

commits.message: [JSI][iOS] Keep Swift symbol names in the prebuilt framework (#50698)
commits.author: tsapeta
commits.pr_title: [JSI][iOS] Keep Swift symbol names in the prebuilt framework
commits.pr_body:
# Why

Crash reports symbolicated on the device (MetricKit with `dladdr`, and the upcoming iOS 27 crash reporter extension) show no function names for `ExpoModulesJSI` frames. With `dwarf-with-dsym`, Xcode's default `STRIP_SWIFT_SYMBOLS=YES` runs `strip -T`, which turns every non-exported Swift symbol into `<redacted>` (1,150 in the device binary).

Only JSI for now. The long-term plan is server-side symbolication with dSYMs, and the other prebuilt frameworks are the same binary for every app on a release, so Expo can host their dSYMs. JSI is built on the customer's machine, so its dSYM (probably a different UUID per build) has to come from the customer's build, and it lands in `XCFrameworkIntermediates` where a `*.app.dSYM` upload misses it. Names in the binary are the fallback, and JSI is on every JS-to-native call. It's also cheap here: +254 KB, compared to +1.1 MB for `ExpoModulesCore`.

# How

`STRIP_SWIFT_SYMBOLS=NO` in `build-xcframework.sh`. The dSYM stays, since file/line and inlined frames come only from DWARF.

# Test Plan

Clean `iphoneos` builds before and after: `__TEXT` is identical, the binary grows from 510,464 to 764,232 bytes (all `__LINKEDIT`), no `<redacted>` symbols left, same build time. In a Release device build of a test app, the embedded framework keeps the same symbol table (CocoaPods only runs `lipo` on it).

Not verified: `xcodebuild archive`, App Store processing, a device crash.

commits.author: alanjhughes
commits.pr_title: [web][audio] Handle blocked play() calls on web
commits.pr_body:
# Why
Closes #36264. 

On web, AudioPlayer.play() ignored the promise from HTMLMediaElement.play(). When the browser blocks playback because the user has not interacted with the page yet, the promise rejects and the app gets an uncaught NotAllowedError. The player also set isPlaying to true before the result was known. So player.playing stayed true while no sound played, and the app received no status update.

- AudioPlayer.web.ts: play() now catches the rejection. It sets isPlaying back to false, stops sampling, and sends a playbackStatusUpdate with playing: false and error set to the browser's message.

# Why

`@Union` decodes by trying each case with `try? Payload.decode(...)`, so every case that doesn't match throws an error that is then discarded. expo/expo-modules-macros#64 makes the generated code skip such cases with a cheap check first; this adds what that check reads.

# How

`JavaScriptDecodable` gets `decodableKinds`, the `JavaScriptValueKinds` that `decode` can accept. It's a protocol requirement with a default of `.all`, so existing conformers are unaffected and generic code (`Optional`, `Array`, a union payload) dispatches to the overrides. commits.pr_title: [core] Fix `SharedObject.release()` throwing on frozen shared objects
commits.pr_body:
# Why

React Native deep-freezes view props in development, so a shared object passed as a prop is frozen by the time its owner calls `release()`. Hermes can't reset the native state on a frozen object, and `release()` throws "failed to define internal native state property". For example, a `useImage` `ImageRef` used as an `expo-maps` marker icon throws on unmount and takes down the tree.

Fixes #50962

# How

Resetting the native state in `release()` is now best effort. The native object is already released by then, and calling the releaser again later is a no-op since IDs are never reused. That's all Android needs, as its native state only holds the ID.

On iOS, a frozen object's native state would still link the released native object and the frozen JS object. `SharedObjectNativeState` now has a released flag, and lookups in both directions skip a released state: `SharedObject.native(from:)` throws `NotFoundException`, events are no longer emitted to the frozen JS object, and returning the native object to JS again pairs it with a new JS object instead of the released one. The native state keeps owning the native object, so a frozen object keeps it alive until GC, same as before. Since all runtimes share one native state, a release now makes the object unresolvable in every runtime, not only the one that released it.
